A1.justification: Both readable 14-page PDFs describe the same HyperET work. Pages 2–14 have identical extracted text and rendered images. Neither supplied PDF contains appendices; both reference supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: v1 reports original HyperET experiments on ScienceQA and 12 MLLM benchmarks, with results in Tables 1–2 and ablations in Tables 3–5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–5 and the hyperbolic-radius analysis in Figure 2.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same hyperbolic radius adjustment procedure, Möbius operations, and diagonal, block-diagonal, banded, and full scaling matrices. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ScienceQA fine-tuning and the same 12 MLLM benchmarks listed in Table 2. No datasets, tasks, or evaluation scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same LLaVA, LaVIN, MemVP, LLaVA-1.5, and LLaVA-Next comparisons. Comparator membership and Euclidean-space controls in Tables 3–5 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.4 retain identical experimental settings, including the ScienceQA test setup, 7B/13B language-model configurations, evaluation metrics, and matched-parameter controls.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical analyses of matrix flexibility, Euclidean versus hyperbolic training, Möbius multiplication, and alternative vision encoders in Tables 3–5. Figure 2's radius analysis is unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the curves in Figure 2 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains the 94.72 ScienceQA average for MemVP plus HyperET with LLaMA-13B.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 1–2, Equations 1–13, and Section 4.3 derivation are identical. No theoretical statement or mathematical reasoning changes in the supplied PDFs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about bridging granularity gaps through hyperbolic radius adjustment and improving pre-training and fine-tuning with less than 1% additional parameters.

C2.justification: Sections 5.3–5.4 retain the same explanations attributing gains to hyperbolic radius adjustment and the same overfitting concern when increasing matrix flexibility. No interpretations or limitations are added.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and a link to the godlin-sjtu/HyperET GitHub repository in the abstract; v1 provides no such code location. Other implementation and hardware disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning statements, and all 71 references are unchanged. The added implementation link does not alter the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: A code-availability sentence is appended to the abstract, and the arXiv version/date marker is updated. The remaining prose, terminology, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added colored code hyperlink causes limited reflow within the abstract. Figures 1–2, Tables 1–5, their captions, and all page layouts after the first page remain visually identical.

improvement.justification: The new code location modestly improves reproducibility documentation by giving readers an explicit route to the implementation. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's completeness or usability, so the supported benefit is limited to improved access guidance.
